prologue.title: Last Performance
prologue.narrator: The rain has fallen on Valmire for so long that even coming back feels like arriving.
prologue.text:
The train slows to a stop in the rain.

You step down onto the platform alone.

The station seems normal.

Old.

Weary.

But normal.

A few travelers still wait beneath the yellow lamps.

None of them really looks at you.

A strange feeling runs through you.

As if you had arrived somewhere no one was truly expecting you.

Alone.

Lost.

You study the invitation in your hand.

> "The Valmire Theater invites you to the final performance."

Your name is written on the back.

You don't recognize the handwriting.

Far off, slow music echoes through the city.

For a second, you have the odd impression that you have heard this rain before.

voyageurs.title: The Travelers
voyageurs.narrator: People sometimes avoid the eyes of those who arrive.
voyageurs.text:
The few travelers here seem nervous.

A woman quickly folds her newspaper as you approach.

A man keeps checking the clock.

11:17.

You notice that no one boards the train that has only just arrived.

invitation.title: The Invitation
invitation.narrator: Some invitations are more like summonses.
invitation.text:
The paper is old.

Very old.

The ink looks newer, though.

On the back of the invitation, beneath your name, a half-erased sentence appears:

> "Do not miss the final act."

train.title: The Train
train.narrator: Leaving is sometimes harder than arriving.
train.text:
You walk toward the train.

The doors are shut.

The driver is gone.

The lights go out slowly, carriage after carriage.

Then the train pulls away into the night.

Empty.

rue_principale.title: The Streets of Valmire
rue_principale.narrator: Valmire seems suspended between two eras.
rue_principale.text:
The streets are quiet.

Too quiet.

Yellow posters cover the walls.

All of them announce the same thing:

> FINAL PERFORMANCE

The townspeople seem polite.

But tired.

As if they had been sleeping badly for a very long time.

choices.text: Follow the music to the theater
Avoid the theater and wander aimlessly

cafe.title: The Travelers' Café
cafe.narrator: Some towns hide their secrets behind music.
cafe.text:
The café is warm.

A pianist plays a slow melody.

The patrons speak in low voices.

You notice several watches stopped at the same hour.

choices.text: Stay at the café and ignore the theater

pianiste.title: The Pianist
pianiste.narrator: Artists sometimes notice what others overlook.
pianiste.text:
The pianist keeps playing without raising his eyes.

> "This town loves sad stories."

Then:

> "People come here to forget certain things."

He pauses for a second.

> "Or to remember them."

choices.text: Go back to the town center

hotel.title: The Valmire Hotel
hotel.narrator: Hotels keep the traces of those who passed through.
hotel.text:
The receptionist smiles at you right away.

As if he had been expecting you.

> "Will you be staying for the performance?"

choices.text: Why does everyone talk about the theater?

hotel_suite.title: The Room
hotel_suite.narrator: The nights in Valmire seem longer than elsewhere.
hotel_suite.text:
Your room overlooks the theater.

In the night:
- you hear applause,
- footsteps in the corridor,
- then silence.

When you open the door:

The corridor is empty.

choices.text: Watch the theater from the window

clinique.title: The Abandoned Clinic
clinique.text:
The clinic seems to have been abandoned long ago.

Medical files still lie scattered in the offices.

All of them speak of:
- insomnia,
- obsessions,
- memory loss,
- and a play called The King in Yellow.

choices.text: Look for the name of the theater
Search the cabinets for a treatment

theatre.title: The Valmire Theater
theatre.text:
The building is magnificent.

Almost unreal in the rain.

Inside, a receptionist smiles at you softly.

> "Welcome to Valmire."

manuscrit.title: The Manuscript
manuscrit.narrator: Some stories change depending on who reads them.
manuscrit.text:
The manuscript is old.

Very old.

The play tells of a city that refuses to die.

One sentence catches your eye:

> "The curtain never truly falls."

choices.text: Compare the handwriting with the invitation

coulisses.title: Backstage
coulisses.text:
The actors rehearse in silence.

Their lips move.

But no sound comes out.

At the far end of the backstage area:
- a red door,
- a stopped clock,
- an immense painting of Valmire.

tableau.title: The Painting
tableau.text:
The painting shows Valmire in the rain.

Something seems different.

You could swear a figure wasn't there a few seconds ago.

A figure that looks like you.

porte_intro.title: The Red Door
porte_intro.narrator: Some doors seem older than the walls around them.
porte_intro.text:
The red door is locked.

Yet you have the odd feeling that it was open before.

Or perhaps it is only an impression.

porte_rouge.title: The Second Act
porte_rouge.narrator: The second act is not meant for spectators.
porte_rouge.text:
Behind the door:

An empty room.

Dozens of chairs.

All turned toward a black stage.

On some of the chairs:

Photographs.

Some show you.

At moments you do not remember.

scene_finale.title: The Final Act
scene_finale.text:
As you climb onto the stage:

The lights come on.

The seats are now occupied.

But every face is blurred.

Then the narrator speaks to you directly.

> "You wanted to understand."

fin_silence.title: The Silence
fin_silence.text:
The fire slowly devours the theater.

The rain finally stops.

Before everything vanishes:

You hear applause.

Even without an audience.

fin_roi.title: The King in Yellow
fin_roi.text:
The yellow curtain slowly falls.

Then the doors of the theater open.

A new person walks into Valmire.

Lost.

Like you at the beginning.

oubli.title: Oblivion
oubli.narrator: You can leave a town. Not always what you saw there.
oubli.text:
You leave Valmire before dawn.

Several weeks go by.

Then one evening:

You find the manuscript at home.

Open to a page you don't remember reading.

femme_journal.title: The Woman with the Newspaper
femme_journal.narrator: Some people hide less a secret than a memory.
femme_journal.text:
The woman clutches her newspaper to her.

You catch only the headline before she folds it:

> THE THEATER REOPENS TONIGHT

When you ask whether she knows the play, she answers too quickly:

**"No one really knows that play. We only think we remember it."**

choices.text: Read the newspaper until you feel dizzy

horloge.title: The Clock
horloge.narrator: Time is sometimes a city's first lie.
horloge.text:
The clock reads 11:17.

The second hand moves normally.

Yet the hour does not change.

A man beside you murmurs:

**"It always starts again in the end."**

Then he walks away before you can answer.

choices.text: Keep staring at the clock until the station seems to change

journal.title: The Local Paper
journal.narrator: Newspapers tell what a town is willing to admit.
journal.text:
The paper tells of an old fire at the theater.

The date is partly erased.

It speaks of:
- vanished actors,
- an interrupted performance,
- a director who was never found.

No name is legible.

Except one word, printed at the bottom of the page:

**CARCOSA**

choices.text: Ask the pianist what Carcosa is
Reread the article from the beginning

clients.title: The Patrons
clients.narrator: A shared silence can weigh more than a confession.
clients.text:
The patrons say little.

Each has a cup in front of them.

None is steaming.

A young man scribbles something on a napkin.

When he gets up, you read:

> Don't go tonight.

Then the ink spreads beneath a drop of water fallen from the ceiling.

choices.text: Stare at the napkin until the ink disappears

pianiste_suite.title: The Melody
pianiste_suite.narrator: Some music doesn't stay in the ears. It stays elsewhere.
pianiste_suite.text:
The pianist smiles without joy.

**"This piece isn't mine. No one here knows who composed it."**

He plays three notes.

You recognize them.

Impossible, though.

You are certain you heard them in your dream last night.

But you haven't slept in Valmire yet.

choices.text: Ask the name of the piece
Listen to the melody until you forget where you are

couloir.title: The Corridor
couloir.narrator: Hotels always have too many doors.
couloir.text:
The corridor is empty.

Yet you hear footsteps behind every door.

At the end, a room stands ajar.

A sign hangs from the handle:

> Do not disturb.

Your name is written beneath it in pencil.

fenetre.title: The Window
fenetre.narrator: From some windows, you see less the world than a possible version of it.
fenetre.text:
The theater glows in the rain.

A line of spectators slowly files in.

Then you blink.

The square is empty.

The theater doors are shut.

The music goes on all the same.

choices.text: Watch the theater until the rain turns silent

reve.title: The Yellow Dream
reve.narrator: Dreams are sometimes dress rehearsals for things that have not yet happened.
reve.text:
You dream of an empty stage.

A yellow curtain slowly falls.

Someone applauds.

Just one person.

When you wake, your hands smell of theater dust.

choices.text: Close your eyes and follow the dream to the end

temoignages.title: The Testimonies
temoignages.narrator: Patients often use the same words when no one has spoken to them.
temoignages.text:
The testimonies describe contradictory symptoms.

Some speak of dreams.
Others of a cult.
Others of a disease of the memory.

One detail keeps coming back:

> the music begins before the performance.

A handwritten note adds:

> Perhaps the problem is not the play.
> Perhaps it keeps something else from getting out.

archives_theatre.title: Theater Archives
archives_theatre.narrator: Bureaucracies sometimes file the inexplicable in ordinary folders.
archives_theatre.text:
You find a file on the Valmire Theater.

It mentions a fire.

But the dates don't match.

1921.
1947.
1973.
2009.

Every document speaks of the same fire.

As if it had happened several times.

choices.text: Go back to the streets of Valmire
Compare all the dates until they blur together

receptionniste.title: The Receptionist
receptionniste.narrator: Sadness is sometimes a form of politeness.
receptionniste.text:
The receptionist thinks before answering.

**"No one really knows who wrote the play."**

Then she adds:

**"Some say it was found. Others that it wrote itself. Personally, I think it was simply waiting for its audience."**

choices.text: Ask why it is the final performance

representation.title: The Performance
representation.narrator: The curtain always rises too slowly.
representation.text:
The hall is almost full.

Yet no one speaks.

On stage, the actors begin an ordinary scene:

a traveler arrives in a town in the rain.

You smile nervously.

Then the lead actor speaks your name.

choices.text: Follow the actors after the scene
Do nothing and watch until the end

lecture_suite.title: The Next Page
lecture_suite.narrator: You never read the same story twice.
lecture_suite.text:
The next page describes a city in the rain.

A station.
A café.
A hotel.
A clinic.

Everything seems familiar.

But no passage says clearly what happens next.

Only this sentence:

> The spectator will choose the shape of his prison.

choices.text: Close the manuscript and return to the lobby
Reread the first line of the manuscript

ecriture.title: The Same Hand
ecriture.narrator: Recognizing a handwriting can be more unsettling than recognizing a face.
ecriture.text:
You compare the manuscript's handwriting with that of the invitation.

The letters are alike.

Not identical.

As if the same hand had written both texts years apart.

Or as if someone were imitating a handwriting they knew too well.

Yours.

choices.text: Keep the invitation and leave the archives

acteur.title: The Silent Actor
acteur.narrator: Actors sometimes know their part without knowing the play.
acteur.text:
The actor looks at you.

He opens his mouth.

No sound comes out.

Then he quickly writes on his sleeve with black makeup:

> Do not finish the scene.

Before you can react, he wipes the message away.

tableau_suite.title: The Figure
tableau_suite.narrator: An image should not wait until it is looked at.
tableau_suite.text:
The figure in the painting takes a step forward.

The painted street seems deeper than before.

At the far end, you make out the station.

Then the café.

Then yourself, standing before the painting.

The painting now shows the room where you stand.

choices.text: Back away toward the backstage area

reception_porte.title: The Forbidden Question
reception_porte.narrator: Some questions close faces faster than doors.
reception_porte.text:
When you mention the red door, the receptionist stops smiling.

**"It only opens when someone insists long enough."**

Then she adds, almost with regret:

**"Most people mistake an answer for deliverance."**

choices.text: Ask why she refuses to talk about it

photos.title: The Photographs
photos.narrator: Proof explains nothing. It only makes doubt more precise.
photos.text:
The photographs show you in Valmire.

In front of the station.
At the café.
In the hotel.
Backstage.

In one, you wear different clothes.

In another, you are much older.

On the back of the last photo:

> Once more.

spectateur.title: The Spectator
spectateur.narrator: Stories only die when no one is watching them anymore.
spectateur.text:
You look at the audience.

The faces grow sharp.

One by one.

Every one of them is yours.

Different versions.
Different ages.
Different choices.

Then you understand something you cannot put into words:

Valmire was not waiting for an actor.

It was waiting for someone able to leave the hall before the end.

The theater falls silent.

Very slowly, the lights go out.

Then you notice something.

Above the hall.

A balcony.

You don't remember climbing up.

Yet here you are.

Below you:

- the stage is empty,
- the seats too,
- as if the performance had just ended.

Then, in the distance…

a train.

The metallic noise echoes in the night.

You step up to the balcony rail.

Through the rain, you can see Valmire station.

The train has just arrived.

A figure slowly steps down from the carriage.

Alone.

Lost.

For a second…

it looks familiar.

Then the theater lights go out completely.

And the music begins again.

retour_gare.title: Back at the Station
retour_gare.narrator: Some paths don't lead back. They lead to the same place.
retour_gare.text:
You blink.

The music dies away.

The rain resumes.

When you open your eyes, you are on the platform again.

The train has just arrived.

In your hand:

the yellow invitation.

It is dry.

Unlike you.

acteur_question.title: The Silent Scene
acteur_question.narrator: Silent answers are sometimes the clearest.
acteur_question.text:
The actor trembles slightly.

He looks toward the stage, then toward the red door at the end of the corridor.

He doesn't move.

He writes only one word on his sleeve:

> Later.

Then he takes his place among the other actors, as if nothing had happened.

choices.text: Follow the actors despite the unease

tableau_contact.title: The Cold Painting
tableau_contact.narrator: An image should not have a temperature.
tableau_contact.text:
Your fingers touch the painting.

It is cold.

Not like canvas.

Like a windowpane opening on a rainy evening.

For a second, you hear the station.

Then everything falls silent again.

The figure in the painting is gone.

choices.text: Let the dizziness carry you back to the station

reception_secret.title: What She Won't Say
reception_secret.narrator: Some secrets are kept not out of loyalty, but out of fear of what they would do once freed.
reception_secret.text:
The receptionist clasps her hands in front of her.

**"I'm not refusing to talk about it. I'm refusing to send you there."**

She looks at the doors of the main hall.

**"Start with the play. Understand the actors. Listen to the music. Only then… will you know whether that door deserves to be opened."**

porte_verrouillee.title: Locked
porte_verrouillee.narrator: Not every important door opens in the first act.
porte_verrouillee.text:
You pull on the handle.

The door doesn't budge.

A copper plate is fixed to it.

> Access reserved after the performance.

When you look up again, the plate is gone.

Or perhaps you hadn't seen it properly.

apres_representation.title: After Intermission
apres_representation.narrator: It is often between two acts that real things move.
apres_representation.text:
The actors leave the stage in silence.

No one seems to breathe.

At the end of the corridor, the red door now stands ajar.

This time, no one stops you from approaching.

choices.text: Follow the actors to the dressing rooms
The door seems to be waiting for you. But something holds you back.

fin_dernier_train.title: The Last Train
fin_dernier_train.narrator: Some exits do not lead outside.
fin_dernier_train.text:
You refuse Valmire before even entering it.

You return to the platform and wait for the next train.

It finally arrives.

Empty.

The doors open without a sound.

You board.

The train pulls away into the night.

Hours pass.

No station appears.

Through the window, in the rain, you notice a yellow poster pasted inside the carriage.

> FINAL PERFORMANCE

Your reflection smiles before you do.

fin_oubli_heureux.title: Happy Oblivion
fin_oubli_heureux.narrator: Not all prisons look like cages.
fin_oubli_heureux.text:
You decide not to go to the theater.

The café is warm.

The music is soft.

The townspeople gradually stop seeming strange.

You have a drink.

Then another.

You laugh with people whose names you don't know.

For several years, you never think of Valmire again.

Then one evening, in a town you don't recognize, someone plays three notes on a piano.

And everything comes back.

fin_patient.title: The Patient
fin_patient.narrator: Reason too can become a form of surrender.
fin_patient.text:
You stay at the clinic.

You read the files again and again.

Everything becomes clear.

The theater is only a symbol.

The music, a trauma.

The posters, hallucinations.

You accept the treatment found in the old office.

When you open your eyes, you are strapped to a white bed.

A voice behind the door murmurs:

**"The patient still refuses the performance."**

In the distance, you hear applause.

fin_acteur.title: The Actor
fin_acteur.narrator: By following others' roles, you end up receiving your own.
fin_acteur.text:
You stay with the actors.

You watch their gestures.

Their silence.

The way they all breathe at the same rhythm.

Someone hands you a costume.

You want to refuse.

But your hands accept it before you do.

They paint your face.

They place you before the curtain.

When the light comes on, you already know your lines.

You open your mouth.

No sound comes out.

The audience applauds.

fin_ville_vide.title: The Empty Town
fin_ville_vide.narrator: A place can outlive its inhabitants. Not always its history.
fin_ville_vide.text:
You refuse the theater.

You walk through Valmire for hours.

The café closes.

The hotel goes dark.

The silhouettes vanish from the windows.

Even the rain finally stops.

The town grows perfectly silent.

Then you understand.

No one was watching you.

There was only the town itself.

Far away, in the theater that is nonetheless closed, the music begins again.

fin_spectateur_immobile.title: The Motionless Spectator
fin_spectateur_immobile.narrator: Sometimes the most dangerous choice is to do nothing.
fin_spectateur_immobile.text:
You stay seated.

You don't leave your seat.

You don't speak.

You don't look for an explanation.

The play goes on.

Then the actors vanish.

The sets fade away.

The hall turns black.

Only you remain.

And a voice, very close:

**"At last. Someone willing to watch until the end."**

fin_fausse_sortie.title: The False Exit
fin_fausse_sortie.narrator: You can take the right road and arrive at the wrong place.
fin_fausse_sortie.text:
You leave Valmire on foot.

The road descends between black trees.

For a long while, you no longer hear the music.

It is almost reassuring.

Then the trees part.

Before you:

the station.

The same yellow lamp.

The same rain.

The same train pulling in.

In your pocket, the invitation has returned.

attendre_train.title: Waiting for Departure
attendre_train.narrator: Refusing an invitation is still a way of answering it.
attendre_train.text:
You stay on the platform.

The travelers leave one by one.

The town's music grows more distant.

An hour passes.

Or perhaps only a few minutes.

At the end of the tracks, a light approaches.

choices.text: Change your mind and head for the town

rester_cafe.title: Staying at the Café
rester_cafe.narrator: It is easy to mistake warmth for safety.
rester_cafe.text:
You stay at the café.

The pianist is still playing.

The patrons stop looking at you.

For a moment, Valmire seems almost welcoming.

The performance can start without you.

choices.text: Step outside before it is too late

traitement_clinique.title: The Treatment
traitement_clinique.narrator: An explanation can be a door. Or a trap.
traitement_clinique.text:
In a metal cabinet, you find a box of pills.

The label is almost faded.

> Dissociative disorders.
> Perceptual repetitions.
> Theatrical obsessions.

A treatment protocol lies beside it.

It is signed by a doctor whose name has been scratched out.

suivre_acteurs.title: Following the Actors
suivre_acteurs.narrator: Some paths become roles when you follow them too long.
suivre_acteurs.text:
You follow the actors down a narrow corridor.

No one stops you.

No one seems surprised.

An open dressing room awaits you.

Inside, a costume lies on a chair.

It is exactly your size.

errer_ville.title: Wandering Valmire
errer_ville.narrator: Some towns are not crossed. They deepen.
errer_ville.text:
You walk without following the music.

You avoid the theater.

You pass shuttered houses, dusty shop windows, alleys where the rain seems to fall more slowly.

The farther you get from the central square, the emptier Valmire seems.

choices.text: Keep wandering away from the theater
Look for a road out of town

route_sortie.title: The Road Out
route_sortie.narrator: A town's limits are rarely those you see on maps.
route_sortie.text:
At last you find a road leading out of Valmire.

No signpost.

No cars.

Only trees, rain and black gravel.

Behind you, the theater's music grows almost inaudible.

choices.text: Follow the road to the end

boucle_lucidite.title: Not Yet
boucle_lucidite.narrator: You are not ready. Your mind knows it before your hand touches the handle. Something is missing — a connection, a truth you have not yet grasped somewhere in Valmire.
boucle_lucidite.text:
The door opens.

The darkness on the other side is no ordinary darkness. It *thinks*. It watches you.

And then — a dizziness. A blank in your memory. A suspended moment.

When you come to, you are in the corridor. The door is closed behind you. As if you had never moved.

Valmire is still waiting for you. There are things you haven't really looked at.

choices.text: Go back and explore the town
